prov_p157.name: Ương Ca
prov_p157.lore: Wooded hills and bamboo above a river, terraced for rice wherever the slope allows. Its farmers sing the oldest planting song in the south, and sing it louder each spring to drown the autumn singing from the graves of Lôi Trạch. A grove of lightning-struck paulownia above the terraces supplies the zither makers of Không Mông.

prov_p158.name: Song Khê
prov_p158.lore: Low bamboo country and grass between two brooks, west of the old Lôi Trạch marsh. Villagers cut bamboo, grow rice and keep the joined dippers at the meeting of the brooks, where couples come from as far as Thu Trì. Hornets as long as a thumb nest in the bamboo, and the ruin of a drummers' hall stands empty on the grass.

prov_p159.name: Thượng Độ
prov_p159.lore: Bamboo and jungle along the upper river, where the ferry rope crosses between its carved stone posts. Its people raft bamboo downstream and keep the charred post that shows how near Phượng Minh's raiders came to the Tower's heart. A grove of purple bamboo above the ferry is cut for flutes.

prov_p160.name: Hà Châu
prov_p160.lore: Grass, bamboo and jungle on both banks of a broad river, with the raw new isle in midstream that Thính Vũ and Xuyên Lâm both claim. Villagers fish, grow rice and row out each morning to see whose flag has moved. Lightning-blackened ebony trees stand alone in the meadows, and no one will cut them.

prov_p43.name: Không Mông
prov_p43.lore: The valley mouth around Không Mông Thành: rice meadows, bamboo and broadleaf woods on the hills, nearly always under fine rain. Many of its families descend from the people of Lôi Trạch and still beat the thunder-day drums each spring. A drizzle-fed spirit spring above the city is shared by the Tower's resident disciples and the city's painters.

prov_p54.name: Hạnh Hoa
prov_p54.lore: Mountain and dry steppe along the river below the Tower's southern road, with apricot orchards on the bank and bare rock above. The market at Hạnh Hoa Thị sells the flowers, felt and ore of the uplands, and the sick come to wait for the healer Giả Hồi Xuân. A tin mine and an old stockade of Khải Lôi's time stand in the hills over the road.

prov_p90.name: Lãng Hoa
prov_p90.lore: Grass and wind-bitten steppe on the coast around Lãng Hoa Thành, at the mouth of a river. Its fishers and salt-boilers came down to the shore after the Pirate Purge, and its children still race the spray along the sea wall. A spirit eye of sea air on the steppe behind the city is the province's one cultivation ground.

prov_p91.name: Vọng Hải
prov_p91.lore: Coastal bamboo and grass at a river mouth below low sea cliffs, held by Xuyên Lâm Môn. Its people fish, cut bamboo and keep the cliff watchtowers manned, though no pirate has come in centuries. Armoured scale-beasts dig their burrows in the bamboo behind the town.

prov_p92.name: Phong Đăng
prov_p92.lore: Fertile river meadows, bamboo and jungle on the coast, the best grain land of the Tower's south. The Lục family's carts are weighed first on the great steelyard each year, and the Tower collects its grain tax here before anywhere else. Thunder bamboo grows in the groves, and in the hills above, a small school calls the rain for the harvest.

prov_thu_phan.name: Thu Phần
prov_thu_phan.lore: Quiet bamboo hills inland from the ruins of Lôi Trạch, covered in old grave mounds and held by Thu Phần Các. Few living people stay here besides the pavilion's disciples; the villagers of Ương Ca keep away, and woodcutters come only by day. Among the graves grows bamboo that sprang from roots the tribulation lightning scorched.

prov_xuyen_lam.name: Xuyên Lâm
prov_xuyen_lam.lore: A high shoulder of Kinh Trập Sơn above the rain forest, mostly bare mountain with bamboo on its lower slopes, where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. Its people are the school's guides and their households, and they live by leading travellers through the forest. Above the gate rises the peak where the school tests its new guides.

prov_r19_1.name: Tàng Vân Lĩnh
prov_r19_1.lore: High mountains at the north-western end of Kinh Trập Sơn, with a little steppe and badland on the lower spurs. Clouds pile into its high valleys and sit there for days. No one lives here; miners dig lodestone on one slope in the dry season.

prov_r19_10.name: Tiêu Thổ Hoang
prov_r19_10.lore: Badlands and bare mountain on the northern side of the thunder range, the rock blackened and fused in patches by lightning. Nothing grows on the scorched ground, and herders call it the Tower's anvil. Diggers come for the red-veined stone of its one mine.

prov_r19_11.name: Lôi Minh Cương
prov_r19_11.lore: Mountains and high grassland on the northern ridge of the range, where thunder rolls along the crest for hours after each storm. A silver mine works the lower slope. Herders graze the high grass in the dry season and never sleep on the ridge.

prov_r19_12.name: Hôi Thành Nguyên
prov_r19_12.lore: Steppe, desert and bare mountain beside the Tower's cone and above Hạnh Hoa Thị, dry in the rain shadow. Ash-grey soil fills its hollows, and in the hills lie the buried walls of a city Khải Lôi Môn lost before the Tower was built. A spirit eye of Earth qi on the steppe is kept by the Tower's outer disciples.

prov_r19_13.name: Vũ Thủy Câu
prov_r19_13.lore: Steep mountain and steppe cut by ravines that run full after every storm and dry within a day. A river threads the largest of them toward the coast. Goatherds use the ravines in spring, and its one peak is named for the clear days after rain.

prov_r19_14.name: Thạch Lũng Nguyên
prov_r19_14.lore: Mountain and steppe in equal parts, the steppe ribbed with long ridges of stone like a ploughed field. A river crosses it toward the sea at Lãng Hoa. Herders from the coast graze it, and its peak tells the farmers below when spring has begun.

prov_r19_15.name: Thiên Nhận Lĩnh
prov_r19_15.lore: A block of sheer mountain rising from near sea level to a high crest. There is no level ground on it to build on, and no one lives here. A soapstone mine at its foot sends its stone down to Lãng Hoa.

prov_r19_16.name: Ám Vân Lĩnh
prov_r19_16.lore: High, bare mountains in the middle of the range, where storm clouds gather dark on the crest before they break over the south. No one lives here. Miners dig a black ore on its slopes and leave when the clouds sink low.

prov_r19_17.name: Khởi Trập Nguyên
prov_r19_17.lore: A high mountain upland with grass in its basins, where the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương roam and the first spring thunder is said to wake every creature in the hills. A banded iron mine works the slope near the ridge. The Tower's fort on the highland road has lain in ruins since the beasts took it.

prov_r19_18.name: Phích Lịch Lĩnh
prov_r19_18.lore: Mountains and badlands around Kinh Điện Khoáng, where lightning strikes the ore so often that the smiths forge in the storms. Its only people are miners and smiths, who come for the storm season. A peak above the mine draws the lightning down toward the forges.

prov_r19_19.name: Miên Trùng Lĩnh
prov_r19_19.lore: High, nearly bare mountains in the eastern range, where the cave of Tàng Trập Động opens and the sleeping creatures wake at the first spring thunder. Hunters gather at the cave mouth each year on the day of Kinh Trập. Above the cave stand the broken walls of Khải Lôi's old cave watch.

prov_r19_2.name: Phấn Nham Lĩnh
prov_r19_2.lore: Grey mountains and badlands at the north-western edge of the range, close to the Tower. Its rock is pale and crumbling, and a blue vitriol mine works the foot of the slope. Herders cross it to reach the steppe and do not linger.

prov_r19_20.name: Hải Vụ Nhai
prov_r19_20.lore: Mountains that drop straight into the sea, wrapped in sea mist most mornings. There is no harbour and no village; fishers below steer by its peak when the mist lifts. A rock crystal mine is cut into the lower cliff.

prov_r19_21.name: Kinh Đào Nhai
prov_r19_21.lore: Sheer coastal mountain where storm waves boom in the sea caves under the cliffs. No one lives here. Its cape peak is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east.

prov_r19_22.name: Hoa Vũ Lĩnh
prov_r19_22.lore: High mountains around the rain-flower pebble beds of Vũ Hoa Khoáng. Its only people are the Tower's pickers and guards, who sort the pebbles in the rain. The peak above the mine is named for the sermon under which the flowers are said to have fallen.

prov_r19_23.name: Tử Vân Lĩnh
prov_r19_23.lore: Steep mountains above the purple-gold seams of Tử Kim Khoáng, where storm clouds glow violet at dusk. Miners work the cliffs and leave when the seams glow. A high peak above the mine gathers the lightning.

prov_r19_24.name: Cửu Tiêu Lĩnh
prov_r19_24.lore: The highest ground of Kinh Trập Sơn, around the split summit of Liệt Khuyết Phong. Nothing lives on its upper slopes, and storm clouds sit on it most days. The Tower's disciples drill here in thunderstorms, past the ruin of Khải Lôi's storm camp and a fulgurite mine.

prov_r19_25.name: Thiểm Điện Lĩnh
prov_r19_25.lore: High bare mountains around the Thunder vein Kinh Lôi Mạch, close to Thiên Xu's border. Lệ Tiêu Hồn keeps the vein, and no one comes here without the Tower's leave. An amethyst mine on the ridge is worked under guard.

prov_r19_26.name: Đấu Lạp
prov_r19_26.lore: Grassland and bamboo between the mountains and the coast, below the Tower. Its people grow rice and weave conical rain hats of bamboo and palm leaf, sold in every market of the south. A spirit vein in the meadows is kept for the Tower's outer disciples.

prov_r19_27.name: Hàm Phong Nguyên
prov_r19_27.lore: Mountain, steppe and grass sloping to the coast, swept by a salt wind that stunts every tree. Herders and salt-gatherers pass through, but no one stays. An old fort from the pirate years watches the shore from a spur.

prov_r19_28.name: Bạo Vũ Lĩnh
prov_r19_28.lore: Very high mountains in the eastern range, where storms empty in sudden cloudbursts that send torrents down every gully. No one lives here. The earthquake of 1199 split the stockade on its pass, and it has stood empty since.

prov_r19_29.name: Liên Vân Lĩnh
prov_r19_29.lore: High mountains whose crests run so close together that the clouds over them join into one roof. Nothing settled lives here. Its tall peak can be seen from Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate.

prov_r19_3.name: Vân Thảo Nguyên
prov_r19_3.lore: High grassland and mountain on the northern edge of the range, its meadows often under low cloud. Deer graze the high grass, and herders bring cattle up in summer. There is no village, only summer huts of stone.

prov_r19_30.name: Chấn Thiên Lĩnh
prov_r19_30.lore: High mountains beside Kinh Lôi Mạch, where the thunder is loud enough to shake stones loose. Gold sand washes out of its streams after storms. The ruin of the fort that guarded the vein in the Thunder Vein War stands on its lower ridge.

prov_r19_31.name: Lâm Vụ Câu
prov_r19_31.lore: Mountain ravines filled with broadleaf forest and mist, cut by a river running south. Charcoal burners and agate diggers work its lower slopes. Its forested peak is green to the top.

prov_r19_32.name: Ô Diêu
prov_r19_32.lore: Forest, mountain and grass in the hills east of Không Mông, with charcoal kilns smoking in every clearing. The charcoal feeds the smelters of the iron mine above the village. A peak shaped like a cockscomb stands over the kilns.

prov_r19_33.name: Thanh Chướng Lĩnh
prov_r19_33.lore: Forested mountains standing in rows like green screens above the bamboo country. No one lives here, but woodcutters climb its lower slopes for hardwood. Rain comes to it every evening.

prov_r19_34.name: Xuân Duẩn
prov_r19_34.lore: Bamboo forest and grass in the low eastern hills. Its villagers dig bamboo shoots in spring and dry them for the cities, and cut nanmu timber in the forest above. Xuyên Lâm's guides pass through on the forest road.

prov_r19_35.name: Dẫn Lộ
prov_r19_35.lore: Bamboo forest below the high shoulder where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. The households of the school's guides live here, and children learn the forest roads before they can read. The giant centipedes in the bamboo above are the first danger every guide is taught.

prov_r19_36.name: Phạt Trúc
prov_r19_36.lore: Almost pure bamboo forest on low hills around Đả Diệp Lâm. Its villagers cut and sell bamboo poles but leave alone the clearing of stumps where Xuyên Lâm's disciples train. The rain on the leaves is so loud that in a downpour the villagers talk in hand signs.

prov_r19_37.name: Cố Trạch
prov_r19_37.lore: Low coastal grass, bamboo and jungle at the river mouth where the ruins of Lôi Trạch Thành stand in the marsh. Eel fishers and reed cutters live here; most of the old city's families moved up the valley to Không Mông long ago. The bamboo inland grows over the graves that Thu Phần Các keeps.

prov_r19_38.name: Tảo Điền
prov_r19_38.lore: Coastal grass and jungle on a sheltered shore. Its villagers farm laver on bamboo frames in the shallows and dry it in purple sheets. A spirit spring in the meadows rises and falls with the tide.

prov_r19_39.name: Tiêu Viên
prov_r19_39.lore: Jungle, grass and bamboo in the low inland hills. Its people grow bananas and plantains and weave mats from the fibre. A lychee grove on the hill above is the pride of the province.

prov_r19_4.name: Thiên Mục Nguyên
prov_r19_4.lore: High grassland among mountains on the northern rim of the range. Herders bring cattle up in summer and leave before the storm season. A white jade mine works the ridge, and the peak above it glows in storms.

prov_r19_40.name: Đạo Hoa
prov_r19_40.lore: Low jungle and paddy grass inland from the coast, flat and wet. Its villagers grow two rice harvests a year and fish the paddies. A forest of hanging vines fills the wet ground above the village.

prov_r19_41.name: Ôn Sa
prov_r19_41.lore: Jungle, grass and a small volcanic mountain on the coast. Its beaches are warm underfoot from the fire below, and the villagers fish and gather sulphur. On the volcano's flank lies the sulphur town the mountain buried in 1013.

prov_r19_42.name: Phiệt Hộ
prov_r19_42.lore: Dense jungle along a river mouth on the south coast. Its people float timber rafts down the river to the sea and sell them at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. Old elephants come out of the jungle to die on a barrow ridge in the grass.

prov_r19_43.name: Phù Ốc
prov_r19_43.lore: Jungle and grass along a river near the coast, flooded every wet season. Its villagers live in houses built on rafts that rise with the floods. A Wood vein in the jungle above is wrapped in wisteria.

prov_r19_44.name: Yên Vũ
prov_r19_44.lore: Wide coastal grassland with jungle and bamboo at the eastern end of the Tower's coast. Its town trades fish, grain and bamboo by sea. Wild buffalo roam the grass behind the town, and the herders follow them rather than drive them.

prov_r19_45.name: Mãn Võng
prov_r19_45.lore: Coastal jungle and grass at the western end of the Kinh Trập shore. Its fishers bring in full nets most days and dry the catch on the beach. Crocodiles lie on the wet flats behind the shore.

prov_r19_46.name: Dạ Chúc
prov_r19_46.lore: Jungle down to the shore on the south coast. Its fishers go out at night with torches on their boats, and the lights of the fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. Bats roost by the thousand in the jungle above the village.

prov_r19_5.name: Phong Hỏa Lĩnh
prov_r19_5.lore: Mountains and steppe at the western end of the range, close to the Tower, with old beacon sites on every spur. A realgar mine works the lower slope. The fort that watched the western road has stood empty since the lightning drove its garrison out.

prov_r19_6.name: Tiễu Bích Lĩnh
prov_r19_6.lore: A wall of bare mountain in the north of the range, all cliff and scree. No one lives here; miners reach its one mine by rope. Its summit is one of the first to catch the storms.

prov_r19_7.name: Trầm Lôi Lĩnh
prov_r19_7.lore: A broad mountain mass in the middle of the range, its valleys forested and its crest bare. Thunder here is low and long, more felt than heard. An azurite mine on its flank and a high peak are its only marks.

prov_r19_8.name: Phi Bộc Lĩnh
prov_r19_8.lore: High mountains with a little forest, where storm water pours off the cliffs in falls that blow sideways in the wind. No one lives here. Its tallest peak sends down a dozen falls after every storm.

prov_r19_9.name: Bắc Thú Lĩnh
prov_r19_9.lore: Mountains and high grass on the northern edge of Kinh Trập Sơn, facing the lands of Thiên Xu. The Tower once kept a watch fort here against the Pivot and gave it up at the truce. Herders graze the high grass and keep away from the fort.

prov_p157_lightning_wood_1.name: Tiêu Đồng Lâm
prov_p157_lightning_wood_1.look: Above the rice terraces stands a wood of paulownia trees, nearly every trunk split and blackened by lightning yet still in leaf.
prov_p157_lightning_wood_1.lore: Lightning finds these trees every storm season, and wood that has been struck and lived holds Wood qi with a spark of thunder in it. The zither makers of Không Mông pay the most for the charred ends, which they say give the truest note.

prov_p158_beast_lair_1.name: Hoàng Phong Cốc
prov_p158_beast_lair_1.look: A shallow bamboo valley where paper nests the size of rain barrels hang from the stems, and the air hums from end to end.
prov_p158_beast_lair_1.lore: Spirit-touched hornets as long as a thumb nest here, led by a queen no one has seen. The villagers of Song Khê smoke out a nest each autumn for its grubs and wax and are stung for their trouble.

prov_p158_ruin_2.name: Kích Cổ Đường
prov_p158_ruin_2.look: On open grass stand the stone footings of a round hall, its floor cut with rings of empty sockets where great drums once stood.
prov_p158_ruin_2.lore: Kích Cổ Đường was a small school of drummers sworn to Khải Lôi Môn, whose drums answered the Gate's thunder at every festival. When the Gate fell in 480 the school had no one left to answer, and its last drummers scattered two years later.

prov_p159_forest_1.name: Địch Trúc Lâm
prov_p159_forest_1.look: On the slope above the ferry, slender bamboo with dark purple stems grows in a dense grove, glossy after rain.
prov_p159_forest_1.lore: The flute makers of the south cut their best stems here. The ferry village cuts only in the dry months, saying a stem cut in rain will always sound wet.

prov_p160_lightning_wood_1.name: Hắc Đàn Mộc
prov_p160_lightning_wood_1.look: A few great ebony trees stand alone in the river meadows, each blackened from crown to root where lightning has run down it.
prov_p160_lightning_wood_1.lore: The struck ebony is harder than iron and holds a trace of thunder. Hà Châu will not cut a living tree, and takes only the limbs the storms bring down.

prov_p43_spirit_vein_1.name: Vi Vũ Tuyền
prov_p43_spirit_vein_1.look: In the meadow above Không Mông a clear spring rises in a stone basin, and a fine drizzle hangs over it even when the valley is dry.
prov_p43_spirit_vein_1.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein shared, by long custom, between the Tower's resident disciples and the city's painters. The painters wet their ink stones here and say the drizzle never ruins a picture.

prov_p54_peak_1.name: Quy Nhạn Phong
prov_p54_peak_1.look: A red-brown badland peak above the apricot market, its crest notched like a gate.
prov_p54_peak_1.lore: Wild geese fly through the notch each spring and autumn, and the market of Hạnh Hoa sets its seasons by them. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

prov_p54_mine_2.name: Hắc Tích Khoáng
prov_p54_mine_2.look: Low tunnels open at the foot of a mountain wall above the river, with heaps of dark, heavy tin ore by the sluices.
prov_p54_mine_2.lore: Tin has been dug here since 720 and is sold in Hạnh Hoa Thị for the bronze of the Tower's rain-chains. The ore is washed in the river, and the water below the mine runs grey.

prov_p54_ruin_3.name: Thạch Môn Trại
prov_p54_ruin_3.look: Two tall stone gate pillars stand alone on a mountain saddle over the road, with the outlines of a stockade wall in the grass around them.
prov_p54_ruin_3.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built the stockade to guard its western road, and the Tower kept it after the Gate fell. Once the Pivot's judgement on the Petal Shore had settled the west, the Tower let its garrison go, and only the gate pillars stand.

prov_p90_spirit_vein_1.name: Hải Khí Nhãn
prov_p90_spirit_vein_1.look: On the dry steppe behind Lãng Hoa a shallow salt hollow glitters white, and the air over it smells of the sea though the shore is out of sight.
prov_p90_spirit_vein_1.lore: A small spirit eye of Water (Thủy) qi carried inland on the sea wind. The salt-boilers of Lãng Hoa say it is where the spray flowers go when they vanish.

prov_p91_beast_lair_1.name: Lân Giáp Cốc
prov_p91_beast_lair_1.look: A bamboo hollow behind the town honeycombed with burrows, the earth around them scored by heavy claws and littered with shed scales.
prov_p91_beast_lair_1.lore: Pangolin-kind beasts with spirit-hard scales burrow here and dig up the anthills of the coast. Xuyên Lâm's guides teach their apprentices to roll one over with a staff without being cut.

prov_p92_lightning_wood_1.name: Lôi Trúc Lâm
prov_p92_lightning_wood_1.look: A low coastal grove of thick-stemmed bamboo, where new shoots stand in dense ranks after every storm.
prov_p92_lightning_wood_1.lore: Thunder bamboo sprouts at the sound of the first spring thunder, and its shoots hold a spark of it. Phong Đăng digs the shoots for the table and sells the oldest stems to the Tower's smiths for quenching rods.

prov_p92_minor_seat_p.name: Cốc Vũ Quán
prov_p92_minor_seat_p.look: On a bamboo hill above Phong Đăng an open-sided abbey stands beside a stone rain altar, and bamboo gutters carry water from its roofs down to small terraces of spirit rice.
prov_p92_minor_seat_p.lore: Cốc Vũ Quán is a small school that calls the rain for the farmers of the south and grows spirit rice (linh mễ) on its terraces. Each year it sends a priest to bless the first cart on Phong Đăng's great steelyard, and it has kept clear of the Tower's ma đạo arts without ever refusing them aloud.

prov_thu_phan_lightning_wood_1.name: Kiếp Trúc Lâm
prov_thu_phan_lightning_wood_1.look: Among the grave mounds a grove of grey-green bamboo grows in twisted stems, each joint marked with a black scorch ring.
prov_thu_phan_lightning_wood_1.lore: The grove sprang from roots scorched by the lightning of Hầu Xuân Lôi's tribulation, and its bamboo still holds a trace of that thunder. Thu Phần Các cuts the slips for its poems from it, and no one else may.

prov_xuyen_lam_peak_1.name: Thiết Trượng Phong
prov_xuyen_lam_peak_1.look: Above Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate a thin, straight peak of dark rock rises like a staff planted in the ridge.
prov_xuyen_lam_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through its dark rock. A new guide of Xuyên Lâm must climb it with a staff and no rope before leading a traveller through the forest.

prov_r19_1_peak_1.name: Ngưng Lôi Phong
prov_r19_1_peak_1.look: A heavy grey summit at the head of the cloud valleys, often hidden under a lid of dark cloud that flickers from inside.
prov_r19_1_peak_1.lore: Storms gather over it for hours before they break. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi, and herders on the steppe take its flicker as the warning to drive their flocks down.

prov_r19_1_mine_2.name: Hấp Thiết Khoáng
prov_r19_1_mine_2.look: A cut in a grey mountain flank where iron tools cling to the rock face, and the spoil heaps bristle with filings.
prov_r19_1_mine_2.lore: Lightning has made the ore here into lodestone, and it is cut for compasses and for array-makers' needles. Miners leave their iron tools outside and work with bronze.

prov_r19_10_peak_1.name: Hắc Diệu Phong
prov_r19_10_peak_1.look: A blunt peak over the scorched badlands, its crown fused by lightning into black glass that gleams after rain.
prov_r19_10_peak_1.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its fused crown. Herders say a storm that does not strike it is not a real storm.

prov_r19_10_mine_2.name: Hồng Văn Khoáng
prov_r19_10_mine_2.look: Shallow galleries in a mountain foot expose pale stone shot through with bright red veins, like blood in milk.
prov_r19_10_mine_2.lore: Chicken-blood stone (kê huyết thạch) is cut here for seals, and a seal of it is a gift fit for an elder. The red is cinnabar, and the cutters wear masks against the dust.

prov_r19_11_peak_1.name: Lôi Chủy Phong
prov_r19_11_peak_1.look: A hooked spur of bare rock juts from the northern ridge like the beak of a stooping eagle.
prov_r19_11_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers at its tip, and the lightning strikes the beak first. Eagles nest under its hook and are said to fly out into the storms.

prov_r19_11_mine_2.name: Lôi Ngân Khoáng
prov_r19_11_mine_2.look: Adits in a mountain slope above the high grass, their spoil sparkling with flakes of bright silver ore.
prov_r19_11_mine_2.lore: The silver here is found in seams that lightning has opened, so the miners follow the storms. Silver from it is used in the Tower's warding talismans.

prov_r19_12_spirit_vein_1.name: Hậu Thổ Nhãn
prov_r19_12_spirit_vein_1.look: On the dry steppe beside the Tower's cone, a round hollow of ash-grey soil lies warm to the touch, with tough grass growing in rings around it.
prov_r19_12_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit eye of Earth (Thổ) qi rising through the old ash of the cone. The Tower's outer disciples keep it, and sit here in the dry months when the rain on the cone is too loud for them.

prov_r19_12_ruin_2.name: Hạ Lôi Thành
prov_r19_12_ruin_2.look: In the mountain hollows beside the cone, the tops of thick walls and gate towers stick up out of grey ash hardened to stone.
prov_r19_12_ruin_2.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built this upland city on the cone's flank as its western market. In 352 the cone woke and buried it in ash, and the Gate never rebuilt; the cone fell quiet again, and in 380 Phó Tiêu Tương raised her tower on it.

prov_r19_13_peak_1.name: Thanh Minh Phong
prov_r19_13_peak_1.look: A clean grey summit over the ravines, its rock washed pale and sharp by the storms.
prov_r19_13_peak_1.lore: In the clear days after a storm it stands out so sharp that the farmers on the coast can count its ledges. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi.

prov_r19_14_peak_1.name: Lập Xuân Phong
prov_r19_14_peak_1.look: A broad peak above the stone-furrowed steppe, where the first green of the year shows on its southern face.
prov_r19_14_peak_1.lore: Farmers below begin the year's work when its southern face turns green. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

prov_r19_15_peak_1.name: Vũ Bút Phong
prov_r19_15_peak_1.look: Three sheer points of rock stand in a row on the high crest, like the points of a scholar's brush rest.
prov_r19_15_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in the cliffs. Scholars in Lãng Hoa say a student who can see all three points from the city on the morning of an examination will pass.

prov_r19_15_mine_2.name: Thanh Hoạt Khoáng
prov_r19_15_mine_2.look: A low quarry face at the mountain's foot, its pale green stone so soft that the walls shine where hands have rubbed them.
prov_r19_15_mine_2.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into seals and pill boxes and ground for alchemists' powders. It is carried down to Lãng Hoa on mules.

prov_r19_16_peak_1.name: Thùy Vân Phong
prov_r19_16_peak_1.look: A tall summit in the middle of the range from which dark clouds seem to hang like curtains on its southern side.
prov_r19_16_peak_1.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the clouds that hang on it. The Tower's disciples read the coming weather of the whole south from its curtains.

prov_r19_16_mine_2.name: Ám Thiết Khoáng
prov_r19_16_mine_2.look: Narrow cuts in a high slope expose seams of dull black ore, and the spoil stains the scree black down to the valley.
prov_r19_16_mine_2.lore: The dark iron ore here is smelted for blades that do not shine. The Tower's masters have favoured it since 906.

prov_r19_17_mine_1.name: Ban Văn Khoáng
prov_r19_17_mine_1.look: A cut in the highland slope exposes ore banded yellow and dark grey, like the stripes of the crouching ridge nearby.
prov_r19_17_mine_1.lore: The banded iron ore is good, but the beasts of Phục Hổ Cương make it dangerous, and miners come only in large parties. They leave a goat at the ridge's foot before each season's work.

prov_r19_17_ruin_2.name: Thanh Thạch Bảo
prov_r19_17_ruin_2.look: A small fort of blue-grey stone on the highland road, its gate torn off and its walls scored with deep claw marks.
prov_r19_17_ruin_2.lore: The Tower kept this fort on the highland road for five centuries. In 1041 its garrison was called east to the Thunder Vein War, and the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương came down and took it; it was never manned again.

prov_r19_18_peak_1.name: Dẫn Lôi Phong
prov_r19_18_peak_1.look: A sharp, bare peak above the forges of Kinh Điện, its crest bristling with old iron rods driven into the rock.
prov_r19_18_peak_1.lore: Khải Lôi's smiths drove rods into its crest to lead the lightning down to the forges, and Thính Vũ's smiths keep them. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on it with every storm.

prov_r19_19_peak_1.name: Vân Hải Đỉnh
prov_r19_19_peak_1.gloss: Summit Above the Sea of Clouds
prov_r19_19_peak_1.look: A high summit in the eastern range that stands above the clouds on most mornings, an island of grey rock in a white sea.
prov_r19_19_peak_1.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the cloud sea around it. The hunters of Tàng Trập Động climb it on the eve of Kinh Trập to watch for the first thunder.

prov_r19_19_ruin_2.name: Thủ Động Trại
prov_r19_19_ruin_2.look: On a ledge near the cave of Tàng Trập Động, the low dry-stone walls of a stockade enclose a hearth and a row of collapsed huts.
prov_r19_19_ruin_2.lore: Khải Lôi Môn kept wardens here to watch the cave mouth and keep order among the hunters on the day of Kinh Trập. When the Gate fell, its wardens went home, and the hunters have kept their own order since.

prov_r19_2_peak_1.name: Hạc Đầu Phong
prov_r19_2_peak_1.look: A peak of pale, crumbling rock whose top is white as an old man's head against the grey ridges around it.
prov_r19_2_peak_1.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its pale rock. Herders say it turned white the night Khải Lôi's last head fell, though older songs already call it white.

prov_r19_2_mine_2.name: Đảm Phàn Khoáng
prov_r19_2_mine_2.look: Wet galleries at the foot of the grey slope drip blue water, and crusts of bright blue crystal coat their walls.
prov_r19_2_mine_2.lore: Blue vitriol is scraped from the galleries for dyers, alchemists and the poison-makers of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners' hands are stained blue for life.

prov_r19_20_peak_1.name: Vọng Triều Phong
prov_r19_20_peak_1.look: A steep peak rising straight from the sea cliffs, its upper rocks streaked white by the nesting seabirds.
prov_r19_20_peak_1.lore: Fishers along the coast watch its foot to read the tides when the mist lifts. Water (Thủy) qi rises to it off the sea.

prov_r19_20_mine_2.name: Thủy Tinh Khoáng
prov_r19_20_mine_2.look: Low galleries cut into the cliff above the surf, their walls studded with clear six-sided crystals beaded with sea damp.
prov_r19_20_mine_2.lore: Rock crystal from here is cut for array focuses and for the lenses of scholars. The diggers reach the galleries by a rope path and work only at low wind.

prov_r19_21_peak_1.name: Hải Giác Phong
prov_r19_21_peak_1.look: A sheer headland peak over booming sea caves, the waves breaking white on its foot even in calm weather.
prov_r19_21_peak_1.lore: It is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east, and they bow to it on leaving. Water (Thủy) qi gathers in its spray.

prov_r19_22_peak_1.name: Giảng Đạo Phong
prov_r19_22_peak_1.look: A flat-topped peak above the pebble sluices, its summit a broad bare platform like a preaching terrace.
prov_r19_22_peak_1.lore: The pickers of Vũ Hoa say the master whose sermon made the flowers fall as rain preached from this summit. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock, and pebbles washed down from it are said to be the brightest.

prov_r19_22_ruin_2.name: Hộ Khoáng Bảo
prov_r19_22_ruin_2.look: Low on the slope below the pebble beds, the walls of a guard fort lie half buried under a great tongue of fallen rock and mud.
prov_r19_22_ruin_2.lore: The Tower built the fort in 505 to guard the road to Vũ Hoa Khoáng. A storm in 1102 brought the slope down on its lower court, and the guard moved up to the mine itself.

prov_r19_23_peak_1.name: Phi Lôi Phong
prov_r19_23_peak_1.look: A high, sharp summit over the purple-gold cliffs, where the lightning seems to leap from it to the clouds rather than fall.
prov_r19_23_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through it from the purple-gold seams below. Miners of Tử Kim watch its crest and leave the tunnels when the leaping lightning starts.

prov_r19_24_mine_1.name: Lôi Tinh Khoáng
prov_r19_24_mine_1.look: On a high slope below the split summit, diggers break open the sand and scree to pull out glassy, branching tubes fused by lightning.
prov_r19_24_mine_1.lore: Thunder crystal (lôi tinh), sand fused by lightning, is gathered here for thunder talismans and arrays. The diggers come only between storms and leave their iron at the bottom of the trail.

prov_r19_24_ruin_2.name: Nghênh Lôi Trại
prov_r19_24_ruin_2.gloss: Stockade Where the Lightning Is Welcomed
prov_r19_24_ruin_2.look: High on the shoulder of Liệt Khuyết Phong, a ring of fire-blackened stone walls encloses the hearths of a camp, open to the sky.
prov_r19_24_ruin_2.lore: Khải Lôi's disciples camped here to wait for the storms before climbing the summit to invite the lightning. When the Gate fell in 480 the camp was left to the weather, and the Tower's disciples now pass it on their way to drill.

prov_r19_25_mine_1.name: Tử Tinh Khoáng
prov_r19_25_mine_1.look: A guarded cut in a bare high ridge, its walls lined with violet crystal that brightens faintly when thunder rolls.
prov_r19_25_mine_1.lore: The amethyst grows along the edges of the Thunder vein and takes some of its colour. Lệ Tiêu Hồn allows the mine to be worked only under the Tower's guard, and every stone is counted.

prov_r19_26_village_1.name: Đấu Lạp Thôn
prov_r19_26_village_1.look: A bamboo village where every porch is stacked with conical hats of split bamboo and palm leaf, drying in rows like mushrooms.
prov_r19_26_village_1.lore: The village has woven rain hats since 640, and a Đấu Lạp hat is said to keep its wearer dry for twenty rainy seasons. The Tower's servants wear them, and their brims are left plain and undyed.

prov_r19_26_spirit_vein_2.name: Tân Lục Mạch
prov_r19_26_spirit_vein_2.look: A strip of meadow above the hat village where the grass is always the bright green of a new spring.
prov_r19_26_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Wood (Mộc) vein kept for the Tower's outer disciples. Villagers cut palm leaf on its edge and say hats woven from it never fade.

prov_r19_27_peak_1.name: Lạc Nhật Phong
prov_r19_27_peak_1.look: A peak of red badland rock above the salt-wind plain that burns crimson at sunset.
prov_r19_27_peak_1.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. Salt-gatherers on the coast stop work when its crown goes dark.

prov_r19_27_ruin_2.name: Phòng Hải Bảo
prov_r19_27_ruin_2.look: On a mountain spur above the coast, the square walls of a fort look out to sea, with a fallen signal tower at one corner.
prov_r19_27_ruin_2.lore: The Tower built the fort in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Pirate Purge there was nothing left to watch for, and its garrison was sent home in 810.

prov_r19_28_peak_1.name: Ngọc Trụ Phong
prov_r19_28_peak_1.look: A very tall, slender summit of pale grey-green rock rising like a pillar above the gullies of the eastern range.
prov_r19_28_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs up it like water up a reed. Cloudbursts break on it first, and the torrents from its flanks are heard for miles.

prov_r19_28_ruin_2.name: Sơn Khẩu Trại
prov_r19_28_ruin_2.look: A stockade of stone and timber at the mouth of a high pass, split in two by a fresh crack in the ground that runs straight through its gate.
prov_r19_28_ruin_2.lore: The Tower kept a small guard here on the eastern pass for six centuries. The earthquake of 1199 that raised the isle at Hà Châu split the stockade from end to end, and the guard has not been sent back.

prov_r19_29_peak_1.name: Bích Tiêu Phong
prov_r19_29_peak_1.look: A high summit that rises above the joined clouds of its ridge into clear blue sky on most afternoons.
prov_r19_29_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its clear crown. Xuyên Lâm's guides take it as their mark, for it can be seen from the gate above every cloud.

prov_r19_3_peak_1.name: Lão Lộc Phong
prov_r19_3_peak_1.look: A grassy summit above the cloud meadows, where deer graze up to the very top.
prov_r19_3_peak_1.lore: Herders say an old white stag has grazed this summit for longer than anyone remembers. Wood (Mộc) qi lies in its high grass.

prov_r19_30_peak_1.name: Thần Cổ Phong
prov_r19_30_peak_1.look: A massive round-shouldered summit beside the Thunder vein, its hollow rock booming like a drum when thunder strikes it.
prov_r19_30_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi fills its hollow rock. The guards of Kinh Lôi Mạch say the peak warns them of storms a day before they come.

prov_r19_30_mine_2.name: Sa Kim Khoáng
prov_r19_30_mine_2.look: Stream beds below the drum peak are dammed with rock into little pools, and pans of black sand glitter with gold flakes.
prov_r19_30_mine_2.lore: The storms cut into the gold-bearing rock above, and the streams wash the gold down. Panners work only after storms and pay a tithe to the guards of the vein.

prov_r19_30_ruin_3.name: Thủ Lôi Bảo
prov_r19_30_ruin_3.look: On a lower ridge near the vein stands the burned shell of a fort, its gate tower collapsed and its stones cracked by fire.
prov_r19_30_ruin_3.lore: The Tower built this fort to guard Kinh Lôi Mạch soon after it took the thunder mountains. In 1042, during the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's disciples took it and burned it, and when the vein was kept the Tower built its new guard higher on the ridge.

prov_r19_31_peak_1.name: Thanh La Phong
prov_r19_31_peak_1.look: A small round peak above the misty ravines, forested green to its top like a coiled snail shell.
prov_r19_31_peak_1.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Charcoal burners never cut on it, saying it is the forest's own pillow.

prov_r19_31_mine_2.name: Mã Não Khoáng
prov_r19_31_mine_2.look: Pits in the riverbank at the mountain's foot turn up nodules of grey stone that split open into banded red and white agate.
prov_r19_31_mine_2.lore: Agate from here is polished in Không Mông for beads and the counters of games. Diggers say the bands are the rings of old storms.

prov_r19_32_village_1.name: Ô Diêu Thôn
prov_r19_32_village_1.look: A hill village of soot-darkened houses around a row of domed earth kilns, smoke drifting through the trees in every direction.
prov_r19_32_village_1.lore: The village has burned charcoal since 680 for the smelters of the iron mine above. Its children are said to be born grey, and they wash in the stream only at New Year.

prov_r19_32_peak_2.name: Kê Quan Phong
prov_r19_32_peak_2.look: A ragged crest of red-brown rock rises over the kilns in a row of points like a rooster's comb.
prov_r19_32_peak_2.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. The kiln village says a fire lit when its comb glows at dawn will burn clean.

prov_r19_32_mine_3.name: Xích Thiết Khoáng
prov_r19_32_mine_3.look: Open cuts in a mountain slope expose blood-red iron ore, and a smelter below sends up a column of grey smoke.
prov_r19_32_mine_3.lore: The red ore is smelted with charcoal from Ô Diêu and sent down to the Tower's smiths. The miners' clothes are red with dust, and they are called the red men in Không Mông.

prov_r19_33_peak_1.name: Mộ Vũ Phong
prov_r19_33_peak_1.look: A forested peak among the green screens, gathering a cloud each afternoon that breaks into rain at dusk.
prov_r19_33_peak_1.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Woodcutters work its slopes only until the cloud forms, and are home by the first drops.

prov_r19_34_village_1.name: Xuân Duẩn Thôn
prov_r19_34_village_1.look: A bamboo village where racks of split bamboo shoots dry over smoky fires under every eave.
prov_r19_34_village_1.lore: Each spring the whole village digs bamboo shoots before they break the soil and dries them for the cities. A shoot left to grow by mistake is tied with a red cord and never cut.

prov_r19_34_forest_2.name: Nam Mộc Lâm
prov_r19_34_forest_2.look: On the grassy hills above the village stand tall, straight nanmu trees with golden-grained trunks, widely spaced like the pillars of a hall.
prov_r19_34_forest_2.lore: Nanmu timber does not rot in the rain, and the Tower's halls are framed with it. Each tree cut must be marked with the Tower's seal first.

prov_r19_35_village_1.name: Dẫn Lộ Thôn
prov_r19_35_village_1.look: A village of bamboo houses at the foot of Xuyên Lâm's long stair, with worn guide staffs leaning by every door.
prov_r19_35_village_1.lore: The households of Xuyên Lâm's guides have lived here since the school was founded. When a guide does not come home, the family hangs the returned staff over the door and leaves it there.

prov_r19_35_beast_lair_2.name: Ngô Công Cốc
prov_r19_35_beast_lair_2.look: A damp bamboo valley where the leaf litter rustles constantly, and red-legged centipedes as long as a man's arm move under it.
prov_r19_35_beast_lair_2.lore: Spirit-touched centipedes breed in the rotting bamboo, and their master is said to be longer than a boat. Xuyên Lâm's apprentices learn here to strike with the staff before they see what moves.

prov_r19_36_village_1.name: Phạt Trúc Thôn
prov_r19_36_village_1.look: A bamboo village on a low hill, its yards stacked high with cut poles and its paths ringing with the sound of blades.
prov_r19_36_village_1.lore: Bamboo cutters have lived here since 700 and sell poles in every town of the coast. They leave the clearing of stumps in Đả Diệp Lâm alone, and in a downpour they talk in hand signs.

prov_r19_37_village_1.name: Cố Trạch Thôn
prov_r19_37_village_1.look: A huddle of reed-thatched houses on stilts at the edge of the marsh, with the black walls of Lôi Trạch Thành visible across the water.
prov_r19_37_village_1.lore: Eel fishers settled here in 760, three centuries after the city burned. They do not enter the ruin after dark, and on the thunder-day they beat drums with the people of Không Mông.

prov_r19_37_forest_2.name: Hải Trúc Lâm
prov_r19_37_forest_2.look: A grove of tough, salt-stunted bamboo on the shore, its stems silvered by the sea wind.
prov_r19_37_forest_2.lore: The salt-hard bamboo makes the best fish traps on the coast. Cố Trạch cuts it in winter and soaks it in the marsh for a year.

prov_r19_38_village_1.name: Tảo Điền Thôn
prov_r19_38_village_1.look: A shore village where rows of bamboo frames stand in the shallows, hung with dark seaweed, and purple sheets dry on mats along the beach.
prov_r19_38_village_1.lore: The village has farmed laver since 820, and its dried sheets are sold in Không Mông and Lãng Hoa. Children here are taught to read the tides before their letters.

prov_r19_38_spirit_vein_2.name: Triều Tịch Tuyền
prov_r19_38_spirit_vein_2.look: In the meadow behind the shore a stone-rimmed spring rises and sinks twice a day, in time with the sea out of sight.
prov_r19_38_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein that breathes with the tides. Cultivators sit here at high water, when its qi is strongest, and leave at the ebb.

prov_r19_39_village_1.name: Tiêu Viên Thôn
prov_r19_39_village_1.look: A jungle village under the tattered leaves of banana gardens, its houses roofed with banana leaf and its paths lined with fibre drying on lines.
prov_r19_39_village_1.lore: The village grows bananas and plantains and weaves mats from the fibre. Its people say the rain on banana leaves is the first sound a child of Tiêu Viên hears.

prov_r19_39_forest_2.name: Lệ Chi Lâm
prov_r19_39_forest_2.look: On the grassy hill above the village, a grove of old lychee trees hangs heavy with red fruit in early summer.
prov_r19_39_forest_2.lore: The first lychees of the grove are carried to the Tower each year by relay runners so that they arrive fresh. The village eats the rest and gets fat for a month.

prov_r19_4_peak_1.name: Thiên Đăng Phong
prov_r19_4_peak_1.look: A tall summit above the sky pastures, on which a pale blue light flickers along the crest in storms.
prov_r19_4_peak_1.lore: Herders call the storm light the sky's lantern, and say it is the only lamp lit in the Tower's mountains. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

prov_r19_4_mine_2.name: Bạch Ngọc Khoáng
prov_r19_4_mine_2.look: A narrow quarry high on the ridge, its floor littered with chips of milky white stone that shine in the rain.
prov_r19_4_mine_2.lore: White jade from here is carved into seals and hairpins in Không Mông. The quarry is worked only in summer, when the herders are on the pasture to carry the stone down.

prov_r19_40_village_1.name: Đạo Hoa Thôn
prov_r19_40_village_1.look: A low village of thatched houses among flat green paddies, with fish traps set in every channel between the fields.
prov_r19_40_village_1.lore: The village takes two rice harvests a year and raises fish in the flooded fields. When the rice flowers, no one in Đạo Hoa may sing, lest the blossom fall.

prov_r19_40_forest_2.name: Đằng La Lâm
prov_r19_40_forest_2.look: A wet jungle where vines hang from every branch in curtains so thick that the forest is dim at noon.
prov_r19_40_forest_2.lore: Villagers cut rattan and vine here for baskets and rope. Children are warned not to play in the curtains, for some vines close on whatever touches them.

prov_r19_41_village_1.name: Ôn Sa Thôn
prov_r19_41_village_1.look: A fishing village on a black-sand beach that steams faintly after rain, below the slopes of a small volcano.
prov_r19_41_village_1.lore: Villagers bury eggs in the warm sand to cook them and gather sulphur from the vents above. They moved down to the shore after the mountain buried their old town.

prov_r19_41_spirit_vein_2.name: Địa Hỏa Huyệt
prov_r19_41_spirit_vein_2.look: In a rocky fold at the volcano's foot a hollow glows a dull red from cracks in its floor, and the rain turns to steam before it reaches the ground.
prov_r19_41_spirit_vein_2.lore: A Fire (Hỏa) vein rising from the small volcano, rare in the Tower's wet lands. Few of the Tower's disciples can use it, and it is rented to visiting cultivators of fire.

prov_r19_41_ruin_3.name: Hoàng Diễm Trấn
prov_r19_41_ruin_3.look: On the volcano's flank, roof lines and a market gate stick up out of a field of grey ash and yellow sulphur crusts.
prov_r19_41_ruin_3.lore: Hoàng Diễm was a town of sulphur gatherers, named for the yellow flames of its vents. In 1013 the small volcano woke and buried it in ash; most of its people escaped to the shore and founded Ôn Sa.

prov_r19_42_village_1.name: Phiệt Hộ Thôn
prov_r19_42_village_1.look: A jungle village at a river mouth, its landing crowded with long timber rafts lashed together and the huts of the raftsmen built on them.
prov_r19_42_village_1.lore: The raftsmen float hardwood down from the forest and sell the timber at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. A raftsman who loses his raft walks home, and is not allowed to sleep under a roof until he has built another.

prov_r19_42_beast_lair_2.name: Tượng Trủng Cương
prov_r19_42_beast_lair_2.look: A low grassy ridge strewn with the bleached bones and tusks of elephants, guarded by a herd of huge grey bulls.
prov_r19_42_beast_lair_2.lore: Old wild elephants walk out of the jungle to die on this ridge, and a herd of spirit-touched bulls guards their bones. The raftsmen of Phiệt Hộ say no ivory from it has ever reached a market and come to good.

prov_r19_43_village_1.name: Phù Ốc Thôn
prov_r19_43_village_1.look: A village of houses built on bamboo rafts moored along a jungle river, rising and falling with the water.
prov_r19_43_village_1.lore: Floods come every wet season here, and since 840 the villagers have simply floated with them. A family's raft is its land, and it is divided among the children by cutting the lashings.

prov_r19_43_spirit_vein_2.name: Tử Đằng Nhãn
prov_r19_43_spirit_vein_2.look: In the jungle above the river an ancient wisteria has climbed a dead tree and covered a whole clearing in hanging purple flowers.
prov_r19_43_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi under the wisteria. The villagers of Phù Ốc bring their newborns here for a single breath of its air.

prov_r19_44_town_1.name: Yên Vũ Trấn
prov_r19_44_town_1.look: A walled harbour town on a wide grass coast, its grey roofs and sea wall softened by a fine rain that drifts in from the sea most afternoons.
prov_r19_44_town_1.lore: Yên Vũ grew up in 860 as a harbour for the grain and bamboo of the eastern coast. Its people say the misty rain is the sea's breath, and its sailors will not leave harbour on a clear day.

prov_r19_44_beast_lair_2.name: Dã Ngưu Nguyên
prov_r19_44_beast_lair_2.look: A broad stretch of tall coastal grass trampled into wallows, where great dark buffalo stand with only their horns showing above the grass.
prov_r19_44_beast_lair_2.lore: A herd of spirit-touched wild buffalo led by a bull with horns wider than a cart roams this plain. The herders of Yên Vũ follow the herd for its dung and its calves, and never cross the bull.

prov_r19_45_village_1.name: Mãn Võng Thôn
prov_r19_45_village_1.look: A shore village of palm-thatched huts in the jungle edge, its beach covered in nets spread to dry and racks of split fish.
prov_r19_45_village_1.lore: The fishers of Mãn Võng have brought in full nets since 790, and they credit the crocodiles behind the shore for scaring off thieves. Every catch begins with one fish thrown back for the sea.

prov_r19_45_beast_lair_2.name: Ngạc Ngư Chử
prov_r19_45_beast_lair_2.look: Low waterlogged grass flats behind the shore, where long dark shapes lie motionless in the shallow channels.
prov_r19_45_beast_lair_2.lore: Great saltwater crocodiles bask here, led by a spirit beast the fishers call the Old Log. The fishers leave it their fish heads and say it has never taken a villager.

prov_r19_46_village_1.name: Dạ Chúc Thôn
prov_r19_46_village_1.look: A jungle shore village whose boats are drawn up on the sand by day, each with an iron torch basket fixed at the bow.
prov_r19_46_village_1.lore: The fishers of Dạ Chúc fish at night by torchlight, and the lights of their fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. The Tower has never forbidden them, and the village takes care never to ask.

prov_r19_46_beast_lair_2.name: Dạ Bức Lâm
prov_r19_46_beast_lair_2.look: A stretch of jungle whose trees hang with thousands of roosting fruit bats, the ground beneath white with droppings.
prov_r19_46_beast_lair_2.lore: Huge spirit-touched fruit bats roost here, and at dusk they pour out over the coast like smoke. The fishers of Dạ Chúc say the bats follow their torches out to sea.

prov_r19_5_peak_1.name: Lang Yên Phong
prov_r19_5_peak_1.look: A steppe-flanked peak whose summit carries the ruined platform of an old beacon, blackened by long-dead fires.
prov_r19_5_peak_1.lore: Khải Lôi's signallers lit smoke here to warn of trouble on the western road, and the Tower kept the beacon for a time after. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock.

prov_r19_5_mine_2.name: Hùng Hoàng Khoáng
prov_r19_5_mine_2.look: A short gallery in a mountain slope where the walls glow orange-red with realgar crystals.
prov_r19_5_mine_2.lore: Realgar is dug here for medicines, festival wine and the poisons of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners work short shifts and drink milk after each.

prov_r19_5_ruin_3.name: Tây Vọng Bảo
prov_r19_5_ruin_3.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur over the western road, its towers split and blackened by lightning.
prov_r19_5_ruin_3.lore: The Tower built the fort to watch the western road after it let the old stockade below go. Lightning struck it so often that by 980 its garrison begged to leave, and the Tower let it stand empty.

prov_r19_6_peak_1.name: Kình Thiên Phong
prov_r19_6_peak_1.look: A sheer, square-topped summit of grey rock that seems to hold up the storm clouds on its flat crown.
prov_r19_6_peak_1.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in its cliffs. It is one of the first summits in the range to catch the storms, and herders on the northern steppe watch it for them.

prov_r19_6_mine_2.name: Hàn Thiết Khoáng
prov_r19_6_mine_2.look: A gallery mouth high on a cliff, reached by rope ladders, where the ore lies in dark seams cold to the touch even at noon.
prov_r19_6_mine_2.lore: The cold iron of this mine keeps an edge through rain and does not rust. Miners are lowered to the gallery on ropes and live in it for a month at a time.

prov_r19_7_peak_1.name: Cự Linh Phong
prov_r19_7_peak_1.look: A massive summit over forested valleys, its bare crest shaped like the head and shoulders of a giant.
prov_r19_7_peak_1.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies deep in its bulk. The thunder rolls around it low and long, and herders say the giant is grumbling in its sleep.

prov_r19_7_mine_2.name: Lam Đồng Khoáng
prov_r19_7_mine_2.look: A cut in the mountainside where the rock is crusted deep blue with azurite, bright against the grey scree.
prov_r19_7_mine_2.lore: Azurite from here is ground for blue paint and smelted for copper. The painters of Không Mông buy the deepest blue for their skies.

prov_r19_8_peak_1.name: Thiên Bộc Phong
prov_r19_8_peak_1.look: A high peak whose cliffs pour a dozen waterfalls after every storm, blown into white veils by the wind.
prov_r19_8_peak_1.lore: Water (Thủy) qi runs down its cliffs with the falls. The Tower's disciples stand under its falls after storms to train their footing.

prov_r19_9_peak_1.name: Tinh Kỳ Phong
prov_r19_9_peak_1.look: A tall peak on the northern edge of the range, its crest still marked by a stone socket where a great banner once flew.
prov_r19_9_peak_1.lore: The Tower once flew its banner here in sight of Thiên Xu's lands. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

prov_r19_9_ruin_2.name: Vọng Xu Bảo
prov_r19_9_ruin_2.look: A stone fort on a high spur facing north, its walls pulled down to knee height on purpose and its gate stones laid flat.
prov_r19_9_ruin_2.lore: The Tower built this fort to watch Thiên Xu's border. When the North Star Compact was sworn again at the truce, the Tower pulled its walls down as a sign of good faith, and they have never been raised.
